subject: Proposal: LatticeOps tenant log sunset & SLA carveout
messages:
From: Alex Meyers <alex@latticeops.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-specific log retention request — LatticeOps

Hi David / Marissa,

Quick context: LatticeOps is preparing for an EU procurement that requires 12 months of tenant-level access logs for a narrow subset of events (authentication, delegated admin actions, and API key issuance/revocation).

Our standard understanding is that Redwood retains session/ephemeral logs for 90 days for hosted customers, with longer retention available via preserved-logs add-on or by request. The buyer is requesting a carveout for a single tenant to retain the listed events for 12 months due to a regulator data residency checklist.

Can you confirm:
- Whether a tenant-scoped exception is feasible without impacting other tenants (segregated bucket and access controls)?
- The minimal evidence pack you would provide for SIG/CAIQ + procurement (what artifacts, playbooks, and sample extracts)?
- Rough timeline and cost (estimate is fine for procurement first pass).

I can loop in procurement contacts once we have a proposed approach. Attached is a short procurement checklist from the buyer.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Security Ops | LatticeOps
Attachments: latticeops_procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Meyers <alex@latticeops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log retention request — LatticeOps

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Agree this is a scoped exception request and worth evaluating. A few quick notes and asks so we scope narrowly: 

- Redwood default: ephemeral/session/trace logs are retained 90 days for hosted customers (we do have reserved/archival options for longer retention).
- We prefer tenant-scoped exceptions that only capture the required event classes (auth, admin actions, key ops) to limit exposure and cost.

Can you confirm the volume profile (avg events/day) for the tenant and if the logs need to remain in-region (eu) for the 12 months? If in-region, that affects storage provisioning.

I'll get Marissa and Jonas to draft a minimal controls and evidence pack we can present to procurement. For speed, I've attached our intake template — please fill the top section and send back.

Next steps:
1) LatticeOps returns the filled intake + volume estimate.
2) Redwood sends a technical carveout proposal + evidence list.
3) Sign MSA amendment + DocuSign.

Best,
David Kim
Sr. Manager, Customer Compliance | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_retention_intake_template.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Tenant-specific log retention request — LatticeOps

Folks — forwarding LatticeOps ask. Please propose the tightest-possible implementation so procurement has numbers. Key constraints:
- Tenant-scoped only; no cross-tenant co-mingling.
- Event subset: auth, delegated-admin, API key issue/revoke.
- Retention: 12 months.
- Minimize operational burden + provide SIG/CAIQ/Doc-level evidence.

Questions for the proposal:
- Can we store those events in a separate object store with restricted access for 12 months?
- What data minimization/pseudonymization can we apply while preserving forensics?
- Sampling/extraction plan for evidence (how we will demonstrate deletion at end of retention window).

Thanks — need a draft by Monday EOD for procurement briefing.

-David

> On Sat, May 19, 2028 at 09:14 AM Alex Meyers <alex@latticeops.com> wrote:
> > Quick context: LatticeOps is preparing for an EU procurement that requires 12 months of tenant-level access logs...

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tenant-specific log retention request — LatticeOps

Team — high level technical proposal (draft):

1) Storage model
- Create tenant-specific retention bucket (eu-central region) tagged as "carveout-latticeops-<tenant-id>". Only write events of the three categories.
- Ingest path: routing rule filters by tenant_id + event_type -> write to carveout bucket. No other tenant writes to this bucket.
- Bucket encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) optional; if requested we can provision.

2) Data minimization
- Strip request/response bodies; keep metadata required for audit (timestamp, actor id, action, resource id, IP CIDR prefix).
- Pseudonymize actor id with deterministic tokenization so LatticeOps can correlate without exposing full identifiers in storage.

3) Access & controls
- Role-based access: Only designated Redwood SOC engineer(s) + LatticeOps named approvers can access via a gated retrieval job. All retrievals produce an audit trail.
- Audit logs for access to the carveout bucket retained for 2 years (separate from tenant retention window).

4) Evidence pack
- Retention policy change note (signed by Compliance).
- Sample extract (CSV) of 1% of events showing pseudonymization and schema.
- Access audit logs demonstrating retrievals.
- Deletion playbook: runbook + script that can be executed at t=12 months for the tenant's bucket (and validation checklist).

5) Sampling / proof of deletion
- At t=12 months, run deletion job + generate a Merkle-style manifest and cryptographic hash of remaining objects; store manifest in an immutable store and provide to LatticeOps as proof.

Estimated timeline: 10 business days to provision + 5 business days to validate and produce evidence pack.
Storage delta estimate: low — approximate 18GB/month for the event subset (example tenant; will refine with real volume).

Attachments: proposed_carveout_draft.pdf (design diagram, 4 pages)

- Jonas
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Meyers <alex@latticeops.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log retention request — LatticeOps

Alex — thanks, appreciated. From a compliance perspective we need to confirm a few items before we finalize language for SIG/CAIQ responses and the MSA amendment: 

- Confirmation that LatticeOps will accept pseudonymization of actor ids (we will map back on approved request with audit).
- Confirmation that extracts provided for audits may be redacted to remove PII beyond the agreed event fields.
- Whether the 12-month copy must be immutable (WORM) or simply subject to scheduled deletion after 12 months. (WORM adds cost/ops).

If you can confirm those three, we can prepare a SIG-ready evidence pack (CAIQ mappings + sample extract + deletion playbook). We anticipate a 3-week calendar timeline from intake to signed amendment if there are no blockers.

Marissa Cole
Principal Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: latticeops_mtap-retention_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log retention request — LatticeOps

Alex — summarizing the proposal and next steps so procurement has a single doc they can circulate: 

Proposal summary:
- Scope: tenant-scoped retention for event classes [authentication, delegated-admin actions, API key issue/revoke] for 12 months in eu-central region.
- Storage: dedicated tenant bucket; optional CMK; pseudonymized actor ids; metadata-only retention.
- Controls: RBAC, gated retrieval jobs, immutable audit manifests for deletion verification.
- Evidence: SIG/CAIQ mapping doc, sample 1% extract (CSV), deletion runbook, audit log samples.
- Timeline: ~3 weeks calendar (10 biz days to provision + validation + Docsign).
- Cost: preliminary estimate attached (storage + ops uplift) — see attached matrix.

Next steps for you:
1) Confirm the three items Marissa raised (pseudonymization acceptance / redaction / WORM requirement).
2) Fill and return the intake template (David attached) with volume estimates.
3) If agreed, we'll issue an MSA amendment (DocuSign link) and provision the carveout on sign.

Link to HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/records/companies/8731
DocuSign (MSA amendment): https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-msa-amendment

If you want, we can run a short 30-minute tech walk-through tomorrow with Jonas and Karthik to show the design.

Best,
David Kim
Sr. Manager, Customer Compliance | Redwood Inference
